source: (cd lp-fw/fw-esp32c6 && cargo build --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf --profile release-esp32 --features esp32c6,test_cycle_probe) && cargo run -q -p lp-emu-esp32c6 --release -- --elf target/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/release-esp32/fw-esp32c6 --time-grade t3 --usb-sj file:target/validate/cycle-probe.cap --usb-sj-tried file:target/validate/cycle-probe.tried --usb-host attached --timeout 120s --wall-timeout 2400 --strict-bus --exit-on '[cycle-probe] === DONE ===' --efuse-mac a0:f2:62:87:b4:8c --efuse-rev 0.2

trust.because: the same allocator and the same RAM model as t1 and t2; the harness's 372 memory values are identical under all three grades (`t3_memory_equals_t1`, `tests/harness_parity.rs`) — a time grade must not move a heap byte, and a memory-cost model answers in cycles, never in bytes

the model exists but the contract does not. t3 is structural rather than per-class — a 32 KiB 4-way cache of 32-byte lines at 338 cycles a fill (the mask ROM's Cache_Get_Mode for the geometry, cycle-probe's code_walk for the cost) and 9 cycles of APB wait state (cycle-probe's mmio_poll) — and it is calibrated on the cycle-probe kernels and validated against 92 like-for-like silicon ticks in docs/reports/2026-09-08-esp32c6-t3-calibration.md. What it does not yet have is a stated band it is allowed to be wrong inside, and a cycle model is never exact; `modeled` until that contract exists (M1 P4)
direct load prints no ROM or bootloader banner; the time grade changes nothing about that. M7 owns it

the same host model as t1 and t2. t3 charges the guest's own accesses to the USB block the APB's wait states, which makes the console path *more* expensive, not more accurate: §2.3 of the calibration record measures the emulator's console path at about 1.5x silicon's already, and that is a peripheral model rather than a cycle model
the same pin observation as t1 and t2, from the same fabric and the same decoder. What a time grade moves here is the frame count in a fixed wall of emulated time, which is reported as timing
the same UART0 model as t1 and t2: the bytes are the guest's, a live socket's arrival times are the host's
